_comment: Community-maintained database of well-known EAX-era games, matched by this script's library scanner and used for the install-time game-details notes. schema_version 2: per-store data lives under stores.steam / stores.gog. Contributions welcome via PR — see README.md's 'Contributing to the known games database' section for the field shapes and rules before adding an entry.

games.name: Baldur's Gate: Enhanced Edition
games.eax_status_details: The Enhanced Edition runs on a from-scratch OpenAL engine, built for its native Linux and macOS ports — it never had DirectSound3D EAX to begin with.
games.notes: If you also own the classic build, it's a separate GOG product the scanner detects on its own — see the 'Baldur's Gate: The Original Saga' entry (gog_id 1207658886), which has real DirectSound3D EAX.

games.eax_status_details: The Enhanced Edition runs on a from-scratch OpenAL engine, built for its native Linux and macOS ports — it never had DirectSound3D EAX to begin with.

gog.store_details: The classic pre-2012 build, sold by GOG as a standalone product separate from 'Baldur's Gate: Enhanced Edition'. GOG's catalogue search doesn't surface it, but the product page and existing owners' libraries resolve normally. This build has real DirectSound3D EAX, unlike the Enhanced Edition's OpenAL rewrite.

The classic pre-2013 build, sold by GOG as a standalone product separate from 'Baldur's Gate II: Enhanced Edition'. GOG's catalogue search doesn't surface it, but the product page and existing owners' libraries resolve normally. This build has real DirectSound3D EAX, unlike the Enhanced Edition's OpenAL rewrite. Its EAX 2.0 environmental occlusion historically needed VxD drivers under Windows 9x (per the Vogons Wiki citation for this title), which is likely moot under Wine.

games.name: Deus Ex
games.notes: Deus Ex defaults to its Galaxy audio driver, which this script can't add reverb to (open upstream bug kcat/dsoal#79). If EAX sounds silent, try the community 'ALAudio for Deus Ex' mod instead — a separate native-OpenAL audio path for this Unreal Engine 1 title, set via AudioDevice=ALAudio.ALAudioSubsystem in DeusEx.ini.

games.name: F.E.A.R.
games.restore_details: If EAX audio drops out during large firefights, try the 'Expand Audio Limits' Advanced Compatibility Tweak (256 simultaneous sources, 48kHz) — that's what it's for. An older one-off report (kcat/dsoal#67) described a load failure under Wine, but it isn't universal; if EAX already works you don't need any advanced tweaks.

games.name: Half-Life

steam.patches: MetaAudio (github.com/LAGonauta/MetaAudio, needs MetaHookSv) adds EAX/A3D-style reverb and HRTF to the current Steam build.

games.eax_status_details: The original release used DirectSound3D, but a 2013 update replaced it with a newer audio engine that dropped EAX entirely.
games.restore_details: If you still have the pre-2013 retail release, point this script at that install instead — EAX still works there.

games.name: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas

steam.store_details: There's no in-game EAX toggle unlike GTA III and Vice City. The current build (v3.0 / 'NewSteam') is a from-scratch Xbox-based port; the EAX/NVIDIA splash only shows on a downgraded v1.0, though the EAX Unified code is present in every version.
steam.patches: SilentPatch SA is the usual companion fix. If the stock reverb is too faint to make out, the community ReverbSA plugin ('[SA|OpenAL] Reverb' on GTAForums) adds pervasive, clearly audible reverb.

games.restore_details: For EAX to work under Wine/Proton the game also needs the COM Registry Routing tweak (Tweak C).
games.notes: EAX is used very sparingly here, so even a correct setup is subtle. The clearest place to check is the enclosed warehouse in the 'Robbing Uncle Sam' mission, ideally compared against toggling the audio override off.

games.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines
games.notes: Bloodlines isn't documented (per PCGamingWiki) as having hardware EAX — its sound design is mostly scripted ambience rather than DirectSound3D reverb zones, so restoring EAX may make little to no audible difference here. That's expected, not a fault. (The earlier Vampire: The Masquerade – Redemption, 2000, is the EAX-capable one.)

games.name: Thief: Deadly Shadows

steam.store_details: Runs on a modified Dark Engine build.
steam.patches: The unofficial 'Sneaky Upgrade' patch (works with the Steam and GOG releases) fixes a well-documented multi-core CPU issue and other modern-system quirks — worth pairing with EAX, much like TFix/T2Fix for the earlier Thief games.

gog.store_details: Runs on a modified Dark Engine build.
gog.patches: The unofficial 'Sneaky Upgrade' patch (works with the Steam and GOG releases) fixes a well-documented multi-core CPU issue and other modern-system quirks — worth pairing with EAX, much like TFix/T2Fix for the earlier Thief games.

games.restore_details: EAX is off by default: in-game, open Options, scroll to the bottom, and enable 'Audio Hardware Mixing', 'EAX ADVANCED HD' and 'EAX Multiple Environments' (per Creative's setup guide for the game).

steam.store_details: Delisted from Steam in December 2022, when Epic pulled the entire classic Unreal series from sale. OldUnreal (oldunreal.com) distributes a free, Epic-authorized copy of the full game.
steam.patches: Creative's official 'EAX Library Patch' (uteaxsys.zip, then uteaxdm.zip and uteaxctf.zip) adds full EAX 2.0 reverb and occlusion to the original Deathmatch and Capture the Flag maps — historically mirrored at patches-scrolls.com; verify the mirror and files before installing. OldUnreal's own patches also add a selectable OpenAL-based 'ALAudio' renderer, a strong alternative if you'd rather use it than this script's approach.

OldUnreal (oldunreal.com) distributes a free, Epic-authorized copy of the full game. Flathub's launcher for this game is a separate, actively-changing package, not necessarily the same build.
steam.patches: OldUnreal's patches add a selectable OpenAL-based 'ALAudio' renderer — a strong alternative if you'd rather use it than this script's approach.

games.restore_details: Check the in-game Audio settings: Audio Mode should be 'H/W 3D + EAX', with Low Sound Detail, System Driver and Reverse Stereo all unchecked.

games.name: Arx Fatalis
games.notes: On Linux, the Arx Libertatis engine reimplementation (arx-libertatis.org) is a strong alternative: it runs natively without Wine or Proton, reuses your existing Arx Fatalis data files, and reproduces the game's environmental reverb through OpenAL Soft's EFX out of the box. It's self-contained, so use it or this script's approach, not both.
